collation.description: Collation driving comparison and ordering; defaults to the database collation. Applies to every text and varchar column, so no type lists it.

fields.description: Restricts which units are stored; omitted keeps every field.

name.description: Name of the generated enum type, unique per schema.

string.note: varchar and text are the same storage; the length is a constraint, not an optimization.

float64.note: float(p) with p in 25-53 is a spelling of double precision.

decimal.note: Exact arithmetic. Without precision and scale it stores any value as given.

object.note: json keeps the input text and key order verbatim; jsonb normalizes it and is the indexable one.

array.note: A native array (text[]) is the alternative when every element shares one scalar type.

enum.note: Requires a named type created up front; Postgres rejects an inline unnamed enum.

time_local.note: Plain time drops the offset, which is exactly what makes it the local variant.

date_time.note: Stored as UTC and rendered in the session TimeZone; timestamp keeps no offset at all.

date_time_local.note: timestamp keeps no offset at all; it names a wall clock, not an instant.

duration.note: Three independent components (months, days, microseconds) that never normalize into each other.

timezone.note: No native zone type; store the IANA name and validate against pg_timezone_names.

email.note: The citext extension gives case-insensitive comparison without a lower() index.

ipv4.note: inet holds a host with an optional netmask; use cidr when the value is a network.

ipv6.note: One inet column stores both families; the address itself carries the version.

cidr.note: Rejects any bit set to the right of the netmask, which inet accepts.

uuid.note: Stored as 16 bytes regardless of the input spelling.

binary.note: Variable length with no fixed-size form; large payloads can move to a large object instead.

secret.note: The type offers no protection; encrypt with pgcrypto or keep the value out of the database.

country.note: char(2) fits but blank-pads and compares by the padded value; text avoids that.

char.note: Bare char is char(1); the blank-padding that makes char awkward needs a length above 1.

int8.note: Postgres has no 1-byte integer; smallint is the narrowest signed type.

uint8.note: Postgres has no unsigned integers; smallint covers the whole uint8 range.

uint16.note: No unsigned integers; integer covers the whole uint16 range.

uint32.note: Postgres has no unsigned integers; bigint covers the whole uint32 range.

uint64.note: No unsigned 64-bit type; numeric(20, 0) covers the whole uint64 range.

double_int.note: Bounded by 2^53, so it always survives a round trip through a double.

float32.note: float(p) with p in 1-24 is a spelling of real; it is not a stored precision.

decimal128.note: 34 significant decimal digits, which numeric holds exactly and a float does not.

time.note: timetz stores a fixed UTC offset, not a zone; plain time drops the offset.

ipv6_cidr.note: One cidr column stores both families; the prefix itself carries the version.

mac_address.note: macaddr is EUI-48; macaddr8 is the EUI-64 variant.

uuid_v7.note: Same storage as any UUID; the time ordering is a property of the value, not the type.

ulid.note: 128-bit like a UUID; storable as uuid if the Crockford base32 form is converted on the way in.

base64.note: Stored decoded, not as the base64 text; bytea_output picks hex or escape on the way out.

base64url.note: Same bytes as base64; only the transport alphabet differs.

commonmark.note: Markdown source; Postgres stores the text and never parses it.

html.note: Markup source; escape it on output, not on the way in.

relative_json_pointer.note: Resolved against a base pointer; the leading integer counts levels up.

semver.note: Ordering is lexical unless the parts are split out or an extension type is used.

sha256.note: 32 decoded bytes; bytea has no fixed-length form, so length is enforced by a check.

port.note: No unsigned 16-bit type; integer plus a range check covers 0-65535.

http_date.note: A header wire format, parsed to an instant on the way in. The OpenAPI registry still sources it to RFC 7231, which RFC 9110 obsoletes.

media_range.note: A range admits wildcards and parameters; media_type admits neither.

sf_integer.note: Structured Fields caps integers at fifteen digits, well inside bigint.

sf_decimal.note: At most twelve integer and three fractional digits, which numeric keeps exactly.

sf_string.note: Printable ASCII only; DQUOTE and backslash are escaped in transport.

sf_token.note: A bare token, never quoted; that is what distinguishes it from sf_string.

sf_binary.note: Stored decoded; the surrounding colons are Structured Fields syntax, not data.

sf_boolean.note: Serialized as ?1 and ?0 on the wire, which is syntax rather than a distinct type.
